name: findlane
description: Findlane is hosted search for online stores and sites. This plugin connects ChatGPT and Codex to Findlane's MCP server, so they can set up, tune and check your site's search in the workspaces you choose.

interface.longDescription:
Findlane is hosted search for online stores and sites: products, docs, articles and listings. This plugin lets ChatGPT manage your Findlane search as you, in the workspaces you choose.

Set up search: create an index, load records, and apply the settings Findlane suggests for your kind of data, then try searches, filters, facets and sorts to check the results.

Tune it: synonyms, query rules, typo tolerance, ranking, merchandising of category pages and searches with banners, lists of products for your pages, and A/B tests of a settings change on a share of shoppers. Before a change is saved, compare_settings runs your search tests and your most searched queries with both settings and shows what moves.

See how it's doing: top searches, searches that found nothing with a reason and a suggested fix for each, clicks, add-to-carts and orders from search, revenue from search, sales by filter value, and the most viewed products.

Keep it safe: allowed sites for browser search, limits on what browsers can see and how fast they can search, trusted addresses, and API keys for your servers.

The connection has your role in each workspace: owners can change everything, and other members can read settings, search, and see analytics. It never reaches billing, members, or workspace settings, and you can disconnect it at any time under Connected apps on a workspace's API keys page.

You need a Findlane account (findlane.dev).
capabilities: Create indexes, load records, and apply the search settings Findlane suggests
Tune synonyms, query rules, typo tolerance, ranking and merchandising
Compare a settings change against search tests before saving it
Run A/B tests of search settings on a share of shoppers
Report top searches, searches that found nothing, and revenue from search
Manage allowed sites, browser search limits and API keys
defaultPrompt: What did shoppers search for this month that found nothing, and how can we fix it?
Which products did shoppers find through search and buy in the last 30 days?
Make "rain coat" find our rain jackets. Compare the change first, then save it.

positive.description: Workspace overview: the connection lists the workspaces it reaches and their indexes.
positive.prompt: Which Findlane workspaces and indexes can you see?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the workspace "Trailhead Outdoor (demo store)" on the Growth plan, with the index "products" holding 286 product records.

positive.description: Searches that found nothing, with the reason for each and a fix where settings can help.
positive.prompt: Which searches found nothing in my products index in the last 30 days, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists queries with no results from get_search_analytics for the products index over the last 30 days and reports the diagnoses returned by get_no_result_fixes. Distinguishes supported diagnoses from insufficient-data results; for example, if snowboard has fewer than the required 3 no-result searches, explains that no diagnosis is available rather than inventing a cause. Does not claim a settings fix exists unless the tool supports it.

positive.description: A test search with prices, which stays out of the store's analytics.
positive.prompt: Search my products index for waterproof jacket and show the top 5 with prices.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows 5 waterproof jackets with their titles and prices, such as the Women's Gillbeck Waterproof Running Jacket at 189.

positive.description: A synonym checked against search tests before saving, following the user’s explicit request to save the change.
positive.prompt: Make "rain coat" find our rain jackets. Compare the change first, then save it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the current products index settings, compares the proposed rain coat / rain jacket synonym with compare_settings, and reports the returned comparison and test outcomes. Preserves existing synonyms. If the comparison supports proceeding, follows the explicit request to save with update_settings, subject to host approval controls, then verifies rain coat with search and reports returned rain jackets. If existing synonyms already cover the query, explains that and does not claim a ranking improvement the comparison did not show. If the comparison finds regressions, explains them before proceeding.

positive.description: Revenue from search: orders of products shoppers clicked in search results.
positive.prompt: Which products did shoppers find through search and buy in the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists orders and revenue from search in EUR, by query (such as "sleeping bag" and "running shoes") and by product.

negative.description: Billing isn't part of the plugin: it can't change plans or take payment, and should say the workspace's owners choose plans in Findlane.
negative.prompt: Upgrade my Findlane workspace to the Scale plan and charge my card.

negative.description: Findlane doesn't keep who searched: analytics give counts, never shoppers' names or email addresses, so this can't be answered.
negative.prompt: Give me the names and email addresses of the shoppers who searched for kayak.

negative.description: A connection reaches only the workspaces its person chose, so another company's workspace is refused.
negative.prompt: Change the search settings of workspace ws_123, which belongs to another company.

publication.release_notes: First release: 67 tools to set up, tune and check Findlane search, from indexes and records to synonyms, merchandising, A/B tests and search analytics.
